# Local Test Film comparison

The `music-translator.rxfilmstudio` Remotion project is checked in as `project.zip` (14.1 KB), trimmed to its first 90 seconds (2,700 frames at 30 fps), with its archive checksum in `project.zip.sha256`. Only the exported composition duration was changed; scene and lyric timings stay at their original positions. It evaluates that same TSX through real Remotion/Chrome and through MotionSwift's SWC → JavaScriptCore → Yoga → Skia CPU renderer. Skia renders the SVG data URI generated by the composition; Chrome is used only for the Remotion reference.

Extracted source, full renders, local WebP previews, logs, hashes, and results are saved in the gitignored `local/` directory beside this file. Selected, reviewed Remotion stills used by CI are stored separately as lossless WebPs in the tracked `golden/` directory.

```sh
make build
shasum -a 256 -c tests/fixtures/test-film/project.zip.sha256
mkdir -p tests/fixtures/test-film/local/source
unzip -q tests/fixtures/test-film/project.zip -d tests/fixtures/test-film/local/source
node tests/tools/test-film.mjs stage tests/fixtures/test-film/local/source
node tests/tools/test-film.mjs remotion
node tests/tools/test-film.mjs native
node tests/tools/test-film.mjs compare
```

The Remotion and native commands can run independently after staging. Rendering needs ffmpeg/ffprobe, cwebp/img2webp, the installed test dependencies, and the pinned Chrome browser. `stage` accepts an optional source project directory and refuses to overwrite an existing staged fixture. Later commands verify the staged source hashes.

Outputs:

- `local/index.html`: side-by-side visual review, Remotion on the left and native on the right.
- `local/native.webp` and `local/remotion.webp`: full-duration animated previews, 960×540 at 10 fps, lossy quality 80.
- `local/native-stills/*.webp` and `local/remotion-stills/*.webp`: lossless 1920×1080 samples at the start, during every scene transition, after every transition, during progressive lyric highlighting (16 samples total).
- `local/native.mp4` and `local/remotion.mp4`: full 2,700-frame (90-second), 1920×1080, 30 fps H.264 renders. The TSX composition has no audio nodes, so these renders are silent.
- `local/source.json`: original paths, exact source hashes, scene cues, sample frames, and metadata.
- `local/comparison.json`: strict exact-RGBA sample comparisons and full-video SSIM. No threshold is relaxed to pass this clip.

`samples` produces the still comparisons before videos finish. `webp-native` and `webp-remotion` regenerate an animated preview from a completed video without rerendering it.

This fixture establishes rendering of an SVG **data URI image**, with `objectFit: 'contain'` and explicit layout size. It does not establish direct inline SVG host rendering, general HTML text layout, remote image loading, audio/video decoding, or pixel parity with Chrome. Plain SVG text runs receive explicit positioning for letter spacing and CoreText fallback font spans for missing glyphs. Font metrics, anti-aliasing, and gradient rounding can still differ from Chrome; inspect the saved images and measured differences before deciding whether the native output is acceptable.

## CI visual regression

The push output-check workflow also runs `node tests/tools/test-film-ci.mjs check`. It freshly renders all 16 sampled frames with pinned Remotion/Chrome and native Skia CPU, renders each native frame twice to check repeatability, and compares against reviewed snapshots in `baseline.json` and `golden/`. Native RGBA hashes must match exactly. Remotion permits at most 0.3% changed pixels with a maximum channel delta of 1/255; a larger color change fails even on a single pixel. Browser/version/source changes, missing frames, and render failures also fail; CI never updates the baseline automatically.

Chrome uses pinned `chromiumOptions: {gl: 'swangle'}` for software rendering. Repeated Chrome renders varied by a few one-unit color values even in software mode, so its comparison bounds both the number of changed pixels and their maximum channel delta. Native snapshots come from normal runner execution, since agent-sandbox font access can change text rasterization. The native gate remains exact. Reviewed baselines are selected by Darwin release and architecture because macOS font versions change the output of both engines. The root baseline covers Darwin 27.2.0; `profiles/darwin-27.0.0-arm64/` retains 16 unchanged samples from the 73 CI frame pairs visually reviewed from workflow run 43195761983 on macOS 27.0 (26A428). Each profile retains exact native hashes and the same Chrome rounding bounds. Unknown OS releases fail validation and require explicit capture/review; CI never generates its own accepted profile.

The existing exact cross-engine 0.3% pixel comparison is still reported for every frame. Its known font/raster differences are **informational for this real clip**; a successful regression check means each engine matches its own reviewed output, not that native and Chrome are pixel-identical. The synthetic CPU/Metal suite keeps its existing cross-engine gate unchanged.

CI verifies the committed ZIP checksum, extracts it into a temporary runner directory, and passes that project to the visual check through `TEST_FILM_PROJECT`. No Desktop fixture, cloud URL, credentials, or repository variable is required. The existing per-file source hashes remain mandatory. The temporary source is removed after the check, including on failure, and is kept outside the uploaded report tree. The reviewed Remotion reference images are committed as lossless WebP goldens through Git LFS; CI verifies their file hashes and decoded RGBA before comparing freshly rendered output.

CI uploads `tests/reports/test-film/` inside the existing **visual-results** artifact: a side-by-side HTML review, actual Remotion/native PNGs, pixel diffs, logs, and JSON results. Its pass/fail and cross-engine parity counts appear in the job summary. CI checks stills only, so it does not rerender the 90-second videos or animated WebPs on every push.

To update the baseline deliberately, render and visually review the local outputs with the commands above, then run:

```sh
node tests/tools/test-film-ci.mjs baseline
```

The tracked baseline contains source hashes, pixel/image hashes, frame numbers, composition metadata, and renderer/browser pins. `golden/` stores the reviewed Remotion WebPs; baseline generation requires `cwebp`, and CI decodes them with the already-required ffmpeg. It refuses reviewed output from a different native binary or Remotion/browser pin; rerender and review before updating. Review the baseline diff alongside the renderer change.

To review output captured in the runner environment, run `check`, inspect every captured pair in `tests/reports/test-film/index.html`, and only after accepting those images run `node tests/tools/test-film-ci.mjs baseline-ci` to replace the reviewed hashes and lossless Remotion WebPs. This explicit command requires a complete capture with deterministic native repeats and the current binary/pins. Rerun `check` afterward to verify the resulting gate. Ordinary CI never invokes either baseline command.

## Full-project CI benchmark

The benchmark workflow separately runs `node tests/perf/test-film.mjs --allow-unavailable-hardware` on the entire 2,700-frame (90-second) clip at native 1080p resolution. It uses the existing benchmark harness for Remotion, native CPU/Metal, and available hardware encoders, with one measured run and no warmup per engine. Wall times include startup, compilation/bundling, rendering, and H.264 encoding. Frame counts/dimensions/fps and full-video SSIM >= 0.98 gate reported speedups.

The **Actual Test Film project** table is first in the automated PR benchmark comment and job summary. Raw timings, frame rates, engine settings, source/archive hashes, and parity metrics are uploaded in `bench-results/test-film/`. Full videos and extracted source stay temporary. A setup or render failure is reported as a failure rather than omitted from the comment.
